display.title: Counting the Omer: The Precious Gift of Time
display.summary_short: Why we count each day of Sefirah: time is a precious gift from Hashem that can never be bought back, with the story of a girl who keeps crying over a lost dime.
display.summary_long: A Sefirah talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi points out that during Sefiras HaOmer all we do is count days, and we even make a brachah every night, which shows that every day is worth counting. Each day's number is higher than the day before, teaching that today must be better than yesterday and tomorrow better than today. What we count is time, which cannot be bought, stopped or recovered once lost. He tells of a girl named Miriam who lost a dime: each time her mother gives her another, she cries again over the first one, until her mother explains that she must forget the lost dime and take care of the ones she has now. So too we should not waste time, Hashem's precious gift. Like someone who lovingly counts his jewels, we count our days and fill them with Torah and mitzvos, and Hashem rewards those who use time wisely with long life, as the Shema says, 'so that your days be lengthened'.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem: don't waste it, and make each day better than the one before.
